Wallace Carothers is a chemist. Carothers was a group leader at the DuPont Experimental Station laboratory, near Wilmington, Delaware, where most polymer research was done.
What is the atomic number of Carbon?
Carbon (from Latin carbo 'coal') is a chemical element; it has symbol C and atomic number 6.
In what year was Bernard Arnault born?
Bernard Arnault: Bernard Jean Étienne Arnault (born 5 March 1949) is a French businessman.
In what year was Radon discovered?
Radon is a chemical element; it has symbol Rn and atomic number 86.
In what year was Adenosine triphosphate discovered?
Adenosine triphosphate: When consumed in a metabolic process, ATP converts either to adenosine diphosphate (ADP) or to adenosine monophosphate (AMP).
Mil Mi-26: Mil Moscow Helicopter Plant. The Mil Mi-26 (Russian: Миль Ми-26, NATO reporting name: Halo) is a Soviet/Russian heavy transport helicopter.
Which country is Focke-Wulf Fw 190 from?
Focke-Wulf Fw 190: Germany. Along with its well-known counterpart, the Messerschmitt Bf 109, the Fw 190 became the backbone of the Jagdwaffe (Fighter Force) of the Luftwaffe.
Who is credited with discovering Tantalum?
Tantalum: Anders Gustaf Ekeberg. Tantalum is a chemical element; it has symbol Ta and atomic number 73.
Who is credited with discovering L'Hôpital's rule?
L'Hôpital's rule: Johann Bernoulli. The differentiation of the numerator and denominator often simplifies the quotient or converts it to a limit that can be directly evaluated by continuity.
Who is credited with discovering Sulfur?
Sulfur: Antoine Lavoisier. Sulfur (American spelling or sulphur (Commonwealth spelling) is a chemical element; it has symbol S and atomic number 16.
A key figure of the Scottish Enlightenment, this thinker is often called the "father of economics" and is best known for "The Theory of Moral Sentiments" and "The Wealth of Nations" — who is it?
Adam Smith was Scottish economist and philosopher (1723–1790).
The simplest pnictogen hydride, with the formula NH3, this pungent gas is also a common nitrogenous waste in living things — what is it?
Ammonia is an inorganic chemical compound of nitrogen and hydrogen with the formula NH3.
Linked to smoking, high blood pressure and older age, this silent widening of the body's main artery to over 1.5 times normal size can suddenly rupture with severe abdominal pain — what condition?
Aortic aneurysm is an enlargement (dilatation) of the aorta to greater than 1.5 times normal size.
This gram-positive, spore-forming bacterium was the first ever proven experimentally to cause disease, laying the groundwork for germ theory in 1876 — which microbe?
Bacillus anthracis is a gram-positive and rod-shaped bacterium that causes anthrax, a deadly disease to livestock and, occasionally, to humans.
Present in every living cell and abundant in liver and meats, this B vitamin acts as an enzyme cofactor and takes its name from the Greek for 'life' — what is it?
Biotin (also known as vitamin B7 and vitamin H) is one of the B vitamins - a group of essential dietary micronutrients.
This outdated 19th-century term for what's now called acute or chronic nephritis was marked by swelling and albumin showing up in the urine — what was it called?
Bright's disease is a historical classification of kidney diseases that are described in modern medicine as acute or chronic nephritis.
Chili peppers likely make this hydrophobic compound to deter hungry mammals and fungi — yet it's exactly what gives them their burning, pungent heat. What is it?
Capsaicin (8-methyl-N-vanillyl-6-nonenamide) (commonly) is a toxin that is the main active component of chili peppers and gives them their distinct pungent, "spicy" or "hot" taste.
This woody perennial herb with bright blue flowers is cultivated for salad greens and a root that's roasted and ground as a coffee substitute. What plant is it?
Chicory (Cichorium intybus) is a somewhat woody, perennial herbaceous plant of the family Asteraceae, usually with bright blue flowers, rarely white or pink.

Native to tropical Africa and Asia, this genus of flowering shrubs and small trees in the Rubiaceae family produces caffeine-rich seeds that are roasted and ground into a beloved beverage worldwide — which genus?
Coffea is a genus of flowering plants in the family Rubiaceae. The seeds of some species, called coffee beans, are roasted and ground to brew into various coffee beverages.
These echinoderms come in stalked "sea lily" and free-swimming "feather star" forms, with mouths on their upper surface ringed by feeding arms — what class of marine animal is it?
Crinoid are marine invertebrates that make up the class Crinoidea.
Its genus name translates to 'two-crested lizard,' honoring the twin head-crests found on fossils unearthed in Arizona in the 1940s — which Early Jurassic predator is this?
Dilophosaurus (dy-, -foh-) is a genus of theropod dinosaurs that lived in what is now North America during the Early Jurassic, about 186 million years ago.
Despite common belief, this shocking South American fish belongs to the knifefish order and is more closely related to catfish than its name implies — what is it?
Electric eel are a genus, Electrophorus, of neotropical freshwater fish from South America in the family Gymnotidae, of which they are the only members of the subfamily Electrophorinae.
This U.S. Marine turned professor wrote a 1981 memoir of his WWII combat, later adapted into a Ken Burns documentary and an HBO miniseries where he was played by Joseph Mazzello — who was he?
Eugene Sledge (November 4, 1923 - March 3, 2001) was a United States Marine, university professor, and author.

This region of the upper limb, running between the elbow and the wrist, contains two long bones, the radius and the ulna, and is technically distinct from the 'arm' proper in anatomy — what is it called?
Forearm is the region of the upper limb between the elbow and the wrist. It is homologous to the region of the leg that lies between the knee and the ankle joints, the crus.

This heavy, slow-moving reptile native to the southwestern US and northwestern Mexico is the only venomous lizard found in the United States, though its sluggish nature makes it rarely dangerous — what animal is it?
Gila monster (Heloderma suspectum) is a species of venomous lizard native to the Southwestern United States and the northwestern Mexican state of Sonora.
This perception occurs with no external stimulus at all, yet feels completely real to the person experiencing it — distinct from dreaming, illusions, or ordinary imagination — name this phenomenon?
Hallucination is a perception in the absence of an external context stimulus that has the compelling sense of reality.
The largest of the eusocial wasps, some species in this genus can exceed 50 millimetres in length. What insect is it?
Hornet are wasps of the genus Vespa in the subfamily Vespinae (the vespine wasps).
Representing about three-quarters of circulating antibodies in humans, which type of antibody is released by plasma B cells?
Immunoglobulin G (IgG) is a type of antibody.
Enlisting as a valet named 'Jean' on Bougainville's expedition, this expert botanist disguised herself as a man and became the first woman to sail all the way around the globe — who was she?

Jeanne Baret (27 July 1740 - 5 August 1807) was a French explorer, naturalist, and botanist who is recognised as the first woman to have completed a voyage of circumnavigation of the globe, which she did via boat.
The world's longest venomous snake with an average length of 3.18 to 4 meters, endemic to Asia and widely distributed though not commonly encountered. What is it?
King cobra (Ophiophagus hannah) is a species complex of snakes endemic to Asia.
Used to treat an underactive thyroid and even a severe form called myxedema coma, this synthetic version of thyroxine (T4) takes about six weeks to reach a steady blood level — what's this drug?
Levothyroxine is a synthetic form of the thyroid hormone thyroxine (T4). It is used to treat thyroid hormone deficiency (hypothyroidism), including a severe form known as myxedema coma.
Enclosed in a fibrous capsule and linked throughout the body by lymphatic vessels, these kidney-shaped organs filter foreign particles and house the immune system's B and T cells — what are they?
Lymph node is a kidney-shaped organ of the lymphatic system and the adaptive immune system.

This English silversmith-turned-industrialist partnered with James Watt to install hundreds of steam engines, then modernized the Royal Mint and struck millions of coins for Britain and beyond — who was he?
Matthew Boulton (3 September 1728 - 17 August 1809) was an English businessman, inventor, mechanical engineer, and silversmith.

This large-scale industrial activity extracts everything from coal and gemstones to rock salt and potash from the Earth, providing raw materials that can't be grown or feasibly manufactured — what is this activity called?
Mining is the extraction of geological materials and minerals from Earth's surface.

This European twin-engine military helicopter was the first production helicopter ever built with entirely fly-by-wire flight controls, coming in both troop-transport and naval anti-submarine variants — what aircraft is it?
NHIndustries NH90 is a medium-sized European twin-engine multi-role military helicopter.
What organic molecule, composed of a nitrogenous base, a five-carbon sugar, and a phosphate group, serves as the basic building block of both DNA and RNA?
Nucleotide are organic molecules composed of a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar and a phosphate.
This rare silvery-white metal, discovered in 1802 and named after a newly found asteroid, is part of the six-element platinum group and has the lowest melting point among them. What element is it?
Palladium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Pd and atomic number 46.
Fill in the blank: “____ (born 12 January 1971) is a Danish convicted murderer and former entrepreneur.”

Peter Madsen (born 12 January 1971) is a Danish convicted murderer and former entrepreneur. Peter Langkjær Madsen (Danish: [ˈpʰe̝ˀtɐ ˈlɑŋˌkʰeˀɐ̯ ˈmæsn̩]; born 12 January 1971) is a Danish convicted murderer and former entrepreneur.
Reaching 30 to 50 meters tall and mostly found near rivers and wetlands, this tree genus's hybrid form has proven so tolerant of urban pollution it lines the streets of London — what's the genus?
Platanus is a genus consisting of a small number of tree species.
A single long chain of amino acids is called a polypeptide — string enough of them together and you get this folded macromolecule whose 3D shape determines what job it does. What is it?
Protein are large biomolecules and macromolecules that comprise one or more long chains of amino acid residues.
A canine native to the southeastern United States, intermediate in size between the coyote and gray wolf. For a century its taxonomic classification has been contentious. What is it?
Red wolf (Canis rufus) is a canine native to the southeastern United States.
Mostly used in wear-resistant electrical contacts and thick-film resistors, which rare, chemically unreactive platinum-group metal has atomic number 44?
Ruthenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ru and atomic number 44.
This veteran of six spaceflights was the first Russian cosmonaut to fly aboard NASA's Space Shuttle, on mission STS-60 — who is he?
Sergei Krikalev (born 27 August 1958) is a Russian mechanical engineer and former cosmonaut.
Made simply from ice mixed with fruit juice or purée, plus the occasional splash of wine or honey, this dairy-free frozen treat goes by what name?
Sorbet is a frozen dessert made using ice combined with fruit juice, fruit pure, or other ingredients, such as wine, liqueur, or honey.
First flown in 1967 with its crew sitting side by side under variable-sweep wings, this Soviet bomber earned the NATO codename 'Fencer' — what is it?
Sukhoi Su-24 (NATO reporting name: Fencer) is a supersonic, all-weather tactical bomber developed in the Soviet Union.
What academic discipline studies religious belief from within a faith perspective, focusing on the nature of divinity, revelation, and the history behind organized religion?
Theology is the study of religious belief from a religious perspective, with a focus on the nature of divinity and the history behind religion.

Picture a spider that never learned to spin: these extinct arachnids lacked silk-producing spinnerets and wore an abdomen split into three or five distinct plates. Which order, known from the Silurian to the Permian?
Trigonotarbida is a group of extinct arachnids whose fossil record extends from the late Silurian to the early Permian (Pridoli to Sakmarian).

First described by John Edward Gray in 1821, this family of small feliform mammals spans Africa, southern Europe, and Asia on both sides of the Wallace Line, and includes the genets — name the family?
Viverridae is a family of small to medium-sized feliform mammals, comprising 14 genera with 33 species.
Twice Egypt's Minister of Tourism and Antiquities, this archaeologist has dug across the Nile Delta, the Western Desert, and the Upper Nile Valley — who is he?
Zahi Hawass (born May 28, 1947) is an Egyptian archaeologist, Egyptologist, and former Minister of Tourism and Antiquities, a position he held twice.
Native to Africa and Yemen, this drought-resistant tree species has individuals radiocarbon-dated to over 1,275 years old — what is it?
Adansonia digitata: Species of plant native to Africa.
Brother of a concert pianist and son of an astronomer, this Russian mathematician built the foundational theory of stability in dynamical systems — who was he?
Formed naturally around volcanic vents and on burning coal dumps, this white crystalline salt is mildly acidic in solution and is used as both a fertilizer and food additive — which compound?
Ammonium chloride: Chemical compound. Ammonium chloride is an inorganic chemical compound with the chemical formula NH4Cl, also written as [NH4]Cl.

Native to the Americas from northern Mexico to northern Argentina, this flowering plant genus is the largest in the arum family and includes types nicknamed flamingo flower and pigtail plant. What genus is it?
Anthurium: Genus of plants. Anthurium (Schott, 1829) is a genus of about 1,000 species of flowering plants, the largest genus of the arum family, Araceae.
These chitin-armored invertebrates must shed their exoskeletons to grow and circulate haemolymph through an open body cavity — and may number up to ten million species. What are they?
Arthropod: Phylum of invertebrates with jointed exoskeletons.
With six species native to Africa (and one also found in Arabia), these large Old World monkeys have dog-like muzzles and have existed for at least two million years — what are they called?

This steel-gray, brittle alkaline earth metal is found naturally only in combination with other elements, making up gemstones like aquamarine and emerald, and bonds so strongly to oxygen that extracting it is notoriously difficult — which element, atomic number 4?
Beryllium: Chemical element with atomic number 4 (Be)

Announced at the 1984 Farnborough Airshow and launched by Northwest Airlines, this advanced wide-body airliner added 6-foot winglets and a stretched upper deck to an already-famous jumbo jet design — which aircraft?
Boeing 747-400: Wide-body airliner, improved production series of the 747.
Its name means 'thunder lizard,' and though long dismissed as just another sauropod genus, a 2015 study restored this dinosaur's status as distinct — which one?
Brontosaurus: Genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaur. In subsequent years, two more species of Brontosaurus were named: B. parvus in 1902 and B. yahnahpin in 1994.
Which mammal family includes dromedaries, llamas, alpacas, and vicuñas among its seven living species?
Camelidae: Family of mammals. Camelidae is a family of mammals belonging to the ungulate order Artiodactyla (even-toed ungulates) and the only living family in the suborder Tylopoda.
Publishing a landmark 1912 paper on 'vital amines,' this Polish biochemist helped pioneer the concept now known as vitamins while researching pellagra and rickets — who is he?
Released by OpenAI in November 2022 and built on generative pre-trained transformers, this chatbot is widely credited with setting off the current AI boom. Name it.

ChatGPT is a generative AI chatbot developed by OpenAI, originally released in November 2022, using large language models — specifically generative pre-trained transformers — and it accelerated the ongoing AI boom.

An American naturalist who surveyed wildlife in Labrador, he turned his observations into quick-freezing methods that launched the modern frozen food industry — and a famous brand bears his name. Who was he?
Clarence Birdseye: American inventor, entrepreneur, and naturalist.
Widespread across Europe, Asia, and Africa, this small predatory falcon has occasionally strayed as far as Guam and the U.S. east coast — what bird is it?
Common kestrel: Species of bird. In the United Kingdom, where no other kestrel species commonly occurs, it is generally just called the "kestrel".
Nicknamed the jade plant or money plant, this low-maintenance South African succulent thrives on neglect and barely any water — what's its botanical name?
Crassula ovata: Species of succulent. It is sometimes referred to as the money tree; however, Pachira aquatica also has this nickname.
Designed to replace an earlier delta-wing jet for the French Air Force, this fourth-generation single-engine fighter first flew in March 1978 — which aircraft?
Dassault Mirage 2000: French jet fighter aircraft. Work on what would become the Mirage 2000 originated with the "Delta 1000" project launched in 1972.
In this heart condition, the heart chambers become enlarged and lose their ability to pump blood effectively, with causes ranging from genetics to alcohol and cocaine use — what is it called?
Dilated cardiomyopathy: Condition involving an enlarged, ineffective heart.

First imagined by Olaf Stapledon in his 1937 novel Star Maker and later named for a physicist who explored the idea in 1960, this hypothetical megastructure would encircle a star to harvest its energy — what is it?
Dyson sphere: Hypothetical megastructure around a star. A Dyson sphere is a hypothetical megastructure that encompasses a star and captures a large percentage of its power output.

In this lung disease the walls between the alveoli break down, merging tiny air sacs into enlarged spaces that shrink the surface available for gas exchange and starve the blood of oxygen. Which condition is it?
Emphysema: Chronic lung condition. Emphysema is a condition of the lung marked by abnormal enlargement of the alveoli with loss of pulmonary elasticity.
This Hungarian-American theoretical physicist won the 1963 Nobel for applying fundamental symmetry principles to the atomic nucleus and elementary particles — who was he?
Eugene Wigner: Hungarian-American physicist and mathematician (1902–1995)
This Stanford computer scientist built ImageNet, the vast labeled dataset that ignited the deep-learning revolution in computer vision in the 2010s. Who is she?

Passed down through generations rather than taught in a classroom, this field covers oral traditions like legends and proverbs as well as customs like festivals and traditional building styles — what is it called?
Folklore: Expressive culture shared by particular groups.
Once classified under two different bacterial genera, this nonmotile coccobacillus forms small gray colonies on chocolate agar and has its own colistin-oxolinic acid selective medium — which species?
Gardnerella vaginalis: Species of bacterium. Gardnerella vaginalis is a species of Gram-variable-staining facultative anaerobic bacteria.
Nicknamed creeping charlie and alehoof, this aromatic mint-family creeper is eaten as a salad green in some countries but reviled as an invasive lawn weed in North America — what plant is it?
Glechoma hederacea: Species of plant in the mint family. It is commonly known as ground-ivy, gill-over-the-ground, creeping charlie, alehoof, tunhoof, catsfoot, field balm, and run-away-robin.

Nicknamed for its mole-like digging forelegs and dense fur, this insect widespread across Europe and introduced to the eastern United States is a textbook example of convergent evolution — which species?
Gryllotalpa gryllotalpa: Species of cricket-like animal.

Formally described only in 1983, this helical, flagella-driven bacterium burrows through the stomach's mucous lining and is the chief culprit behind gastric ulcers and some stomach cancers. What is it?
Nicknamed 'Hobbit,' this extinct species of small archaic humans stood about 1.1 meters tall and lived on the Indonesian island of Flores until roughly 50,000 years ago — which species?
Homo floresiensis: Extinct small human species found in Flores.

Typically begun with an induction of preliminary instructions, this state of focused attention and heightened suggestibility is debated as either an altered trance or a form of imaginative role-play — what is it?
Hypnosis: State of increased suggestibility. There are competing theories explaining hypnosis and related phenomena.

This analytical framework describes how overlapping identities like race, gender, and class combine to create unique experiences of discrimination or privilege, and emerged partly as a critique of mainstream feminism — which concept?
Intersectionality: Theory of discrimination. The term intersectionality was coined by Kimberlé Crenshaw in 1989.
A Communist Party member and Stanford-trained psychiatrist, this woman is best remembered for her romantic relationship with J. Robert Oppenheimer, which put her under FBI surveillance. Who is she?

Also called legal theory, this field applies philosophical methods to questions like what the law is and how it ought to be — with roots traced to Confucius, Aristotle, and Enlightenment thinkers like Locke and Rousseau. What field is it?
Making up 2 to 8 percent of milk by mass, this disaccharide combines galactose and glucose and takes its name from the Latin word for milk — what is it?
Lactose: Carbohydrate. Lactose is a disaccharide composed of galactose and glucose and has the molecular formula C12H22O11.
The offspring of a male lion and a female tiger, which hybrid cat is the largest of all living felines and — unlike its reverse-cross cousin — grows larger than either parent?
Liger: Lion and tigress hybrid. The liger is a hybrid offspring of a male lion (Panthera leo) and a tigress, or female tiger (Panthera tigris).
Native to Afghanistan and Iran, this herb tastes like an intensified cross between celery and parsley, with seeds used much like fennel — what is it?
Nicknamed the 'tree of death' and 'beach apple,' this small-fruited tropical tree oozes a milky sap so toxic it can blister skin on contact — which tree?
Manchineel: Poisonous plant from tropical North and South America.

Spanning everything from sacred religious writings to the exuberantly profane, and often grouped by place, language, and genre, what broad body of European writing falls between late antiquity and the Renaissance?
Medieval literature: Literary works of the Middle Ages.
Named from Greek words for 'small' and 'head,' this congenital condition involves a smaller-than-average head size and can result from genetic syndromes or prenatal toxin exposure — what is it?
Microcephaly: Condition in which the head is small due to an underdeveloped brain.
Known as simple sugars, these colorless, water-soluble crystalline compounds include glucose and fructose and serve as the building blocks of starch and cellulose — what are they called?
Monosaccharide: Simple sugars such as glucose and fructose.

First classified by Linnaeus in 1753, this genus in the family Myrtaceae includes only two accepted species today: one native to the Mediterranean, the other to the Saharan mountains of North Africa — which genus?
Myrtus: Genus of flowering plants in the family Myrtaceae.
This Serbian-American engineer designed the modern alternating current electricity supply system—the backbone of today's power grid. Who?
Nikola Tesla: Serbian-American engineer and inventor (1856–1943)
Starting as a metals trader after the Soviet Union's collapse, which Russian billionaire built the Sayanogorsk smelter into the world's largest aluminium company, Rusal?
Also known as jícama or Mexican turnip, this pea-family vine's edible tuberous root comes in a milky-juice form and a watery-juice form — which species is it?
Pachyrhizus erosus: Species of legume. Pachyrhizus tuberosus and Pachyrhizus ahipa are the other two cultivated species in the genus.
Commonly called geraniums or storksbills, this genus of roughly 280 evergreen species was split from a related genus by a botanist in 1789 — which genus, native largely to southern Africa?
Pelargonium: Genus of plants. It includes about 280 species of perennials, succulents, and shrubs.
This colorless, highly toxic pnictogen hydride is pure when odorless, but technical samples reek of rotting fish — and impurities can make it burst into flame in air — what is it?
Named after a French mathematician and physicist, this materials-science measure captures how much a material bulges sideways when compressed lengthwise — what is it?
Poisson's ratio: Measure of material deformation perpendicular to loading.
Found just below the bladder with the urethra passing through it, this male-only gland acts like a muscle-driven switch between urination and ejaculation — which organ?
Prostate: Gland of the male reproductive system.
Sold as Seroquel and prescribed for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, this atypical antipsychotic is also widely (and questionably) used as a sleep aid for its tranquillizing effect — which drug?
Quetiapine: Atypical antipsychotic medication. Quetiapine is believed to work by blocking a number of receptors, including those for serotonin and dopamine.
Native to East Asia but a notorious invasive pest in Europe and North America, this knotweed has won over beekeepers and foragers alike, its young stems tasting of lemony rhubarb. What plant is it?
Native to Eurasia and commonly known simply as the raspberry, this red-fruited bramble is widely cultivated across temperate regions — what species is it?
Nicknamed 'snail fever,' this tropical disease is caused by a parasitic flatworm picked up from freshwater contaminated by infected snails — what is it?
Schistosomiasis: Human disease caused by parasitic worms called schistosomes.

Recognized by the Kennel Club in 1909, this small, clever herding dog breed originated in Scotland's northern isles and was originally called by a different collie name before breeders objected — which breed?
Shetland Sheepdog: Scottish breed of dog. The Shetland Sheepdog, also known as the Sheltie, is a breed of herding dog that originated in the Shetland Islands of Scotland.

Originating in South America and rapidly diversifying after the extinction of the dinosaurs, this plant family — commonly known as the nightshades — includes toxic alkaloid-rich species alongside tomatoes, potatoes, and peppers. What family is it?
Shaped roughly like a necktie and made up of the manubrium, body, and xiphoid process, which flat bone protects the heart and lungs at the front of the rib cage?
Sternum: Flat bone in the middle front part of the rib cage.

Caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum, this infection famously hides: a painless ulcer first, then a rash that loves the palms and soles, then years of silent latency before tertiary damage. What is it?
Named from Greek for 'four teeth,' this family includes the pufferfish, blowfish, and toadfish — many of them among the most poisonous vertebrates alive. What is this family called?
Tetraodontidae: Family of pufferfish. Tetraodontidae is a family of marine and freshwater fish in the order Tetraodontiformes.

Sold under the brand name Zanaflex, this alpha-2 adrenergic agonist treats muscle spasticity from spinal cord injuries and multiple sclerosis, and racked up over 8 million US prescriptions in 2023 — what is it?
NATO code-named 'Careless,' this three-engined Soviet airliner once carried half of Aeroflot's passengers and could operate from unpaved gravel airstrips in Arctic conditions — which aircraft?
Tupolev Tu-154: Soviet and Russian medium-range trijet airliner.

Sold under the brand name Effexor, this serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor treats depression, anxiety, and PTSD, and is also available as an extended-release salt called Venbysi XR — what medication is it?
Once nicknamed 'the poor man's racehorse,' this British sighthound is believed to have the fastest idle-to-running acceleration of any dog breed — which breed?
Whippet: British breed of dog. It closely resembles the Greyhound and the smaller Italian Greyhound, and is intermediate between them in size.
Nicknamed the 'Sleeping Dragon' during his years in seclusion, this strategist was sought out three times by Liu Bei and helped engineer victory at the Battle of Red Cliffs — who is he?
Zhuge Liang: Chinese statesman and strategist (181–234)

Val Kilmer: Val Edward Kilmer (December 31, 1959 – April 1, 2025) was an American actor.
